title: GateDrop: choose the energy *occasion*
dek: A one-page creative strategy specimen for Tim Near. It turns GateDrop's public launch language into two distinct tests without claiming access to private performance data.
lens: Energy gummies · DTC paid social · challenger positioning
sources: GateDrop product page + launch release + founder post

sections.heading: the message *gap*
sections.body:
GateDrop has a sharp category challenger: portable, portionable energy without a can. The current product page then stretches that idea across focus, productivity, workouts, long shifts, travel, and action sports. The first paid-social test should choose one moment of substitution instead of asking the gummy to mean everything at once.

A second issue needs claim governance before scale: the current site and April launch release state 25mg caffeine per gummy, while an earlier founder launch post stated 20mg. Current label truth should govern every ad.

rows.claim: The current product is purchasable and positioned as customizable energy.
rows.evidence: The current page lists $14.99 for a 25-count pouch and states 25mg caffeine, 2g sugar, and 9 calories per gummy.

rows.claim: The owned challenger is the energy-drink occasion.
rows.evidence: GateDrop's launch release says the brand was built to challenge traditional energy drinks through portable, precisely dosed caffeine.

rows.claim: One use occasion per test is the likely creative opening.
rows.evidence: This is an inference from the broad occasion list on the product page. No public account-performance evidence was used.

items.why: Target the caffeine-sensitive or dose-conscious buyer. The enemy is the all-or-nothing can. Show the buyer choosing one gummy, then deciding whether the moment needs another. Use only current, label-approved dose language.

items.action: B · Pocket energy for the long shift
items.why: Target one shift-based use case, not all busy people. Show the product surviving a bag, pocket, car, and break room while a can is impractical. The promise is convenience and format, not medical alertness or safety.

blocks.label: Concept A · control
blocks.text:
A1  Your energy should not come in an all-or-nothing can.

A2  One gummy. 25 milligrams of caffeine. You decide what the moment needs.

A3  The energy format for people who want the dial, not the blast.

blocks.label: Concept B · long shift
blocks.text:
B1  A four-pack of energy that fits where a can does not.

B2  Long shift. Small pocket. No can required.

B3  When the next break is unpredictable, carry the format that is not.

sections.heading: visible *unknowns*
sections.body:
UNCONFIRMED: active paid-social inventory, sales velocity, strongest buyer, onset experience, repeat rate, creator rights, approved comparison language, and production capacity.

CLAIM HOLD: reconcile the older 20mg founder post with the current 25mg product page and label before any asset uses a number. Avoid claims about being safer, healthier, crash-free, faster acting, or equivalent to a named energy drink unless the brand supplies substantiation and approval.

ledger.used_for: Founder language and historical dose discrepancy
